title: Qatar to Philippines remittance: onboarding and screening decision rules
notes: VERSION 0.2. Rules that cite a section of the QCB AML/CFT Instructions (May 2020, published by QFIU), Law No. 20 of 2019, the QFCRA Guidance on Sanctions (2025) or BSP issuances were drafted from the primary text. Rules whose basis says 'firm policy' or 'confirm' are judgement placeholders. NOT reviewed by a compliance professional. Thresholds and document lists must still be confirmed against the current QCB instructions and the firm's own risk assessment before use.
sources: Qatar Central Bank, AML/CFT Instructions (May 2020, English), published by the Qatar Financial Information Unit: items 6.7 (outsourcing), 10.4 (persons in sanctions lists: no relationship or transaction, within 24 hours; STR; inform QCB), 14.12 (linked one-off transactions and the QR 50,000 CDD threshold), 15.2 (customer identification data for individuals), 18 (MVTS and wire transfers: QR 3,500, full originator and recipient information cross-border, prohibition on listed persons at any value, charitable causes need prior approval, 10-year retention), 19.5 (STR immediately, by the MLRO, irrespective of amount)

State of Qatar, Law No. 20 of 2019 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing: 10-year record keeping; CDD on occasional transactions at the threshold in the Implementing Regulation; wire transfers (Art. 18); DNFBP definition

Qatar Financial Centre Regulatory Authority, Guidance on the Implementation of an Effective Sanctions Compliance Programme (2025): screen immediately after publication of UNSC, NCTC domestic alerts or PPO orders; fuzzy matching calibrated to risk; keep records of all alerts including cleared false positives

Qatar National Counter Terrorism Committee, Unified Record of Persons and Entities on the Sanction List (Ministry of Interior portal, JSON, loaded as source QA_NCTC): UNSC designations as applied in Qatar plus domestic designations by Public Prosecutor order, with QID and passport numbers

Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, Circular No. 1206 (2024), Consolidated Rules for Money Service Businesses: large value pay-outs above PHP 500,000 require enhanced due diligence and payment only by cheque or credit to an account

Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, Circular No. 608 (2008), valid identification cards for financial transactions: one valid photo-bearing ID issued by an official authority for a first transaction; student beneficiaries may use a signed school ID
Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, Memorandum M-2025-012: all formats of the Philippine National ID (card, paper, digital) accepted in financial transactions
Anti-Money Laundering Council (Philippines): covered transaction reports above PHP 500,000 within five working days; STR timelines per AMLC regulations (confirm current deadline)
FATF Recommendations 6, 10, 12, 14, 16 and the FATF list of High-Risk Jurisdictions subject to a Call for Action (current list)
Qatar ID number structure (century digit, birth year, ISO numeric nationality); PhilSys Card Number format (Philippine Statistics Authority)

national_lists: Qatar NCTC unified record incl. domestic designations by Public Prosecutor order (source QA_NCTC, loaded)

documents.label: Qatar ID card (QID)
documents.notes: Primary ID for residents. Number encodes birth year and nationality; cross-checked against stated DOB and nationality.

documents.label: Passport
documents.notes: Accepted with a valid Qatar visa or entry for non-residents; MRZ verified.

sending.notes: QCB Instructions 15.2: identification data for individuals must include full name, aliases, permanent address, contact details, profession, work address, nationality, QID number for Qataris and residents or passport number for non-residents, date and place of birth, sponsor name and address, and purpose of the relationship; verified from a valid official document. Most senders are migrant workers paid under the Wage Protection System.

documents.label: Philippine National ID / PhilID / ePhilID (any format)
School ID signed by the principal (beneficiaries below voting age only)

receiving.notes: BSP Circular 608: a first-time claimant presents one valid photo-bearing ID from an official authority. Circular 1206: pay-outs above PHP 500,000 need enhanced due diligence and go by cheque or account credit only. Sender-side record must carry full originator and beneficiary information (QCB 18(6), FATF R.16).

rules.title: Listed person: UNSC or Qatar NCTC designation confirmed
rules.reason: High-confidence name match with agreeing date of birth on a UNSC, NCTC or other sanctions list. QCB Instructions 10.4: do not establish or continue the relationship or carry out the transaction, within 24 hours; make an STR to the FIU; inform QCB within 24 hours. 18(9): no transaction of any value.
rules.basis: QCB AML/CFT Instructions 10.4, 18(9); Law 20/2019 targeted financial sanctions; FATF R.6

rules.title: Customer's ID number appears on a list
rules.reason: The customer's Qatar ID or passport number appears on the NCTC unified record. This is an exact identifier match, not a name similarity. QCB 10.4 applies: no transaction, STR, inform QCB within 24 hours.
rules.basis: QCB AML/CFT Instructions 10.4, 18(9); NCTC unified record carries QID and passport numbers

rules.title: High-confidence match, DOB not comparable
rules.reason: High-confidence name match but the list entry or the customer has no date of birth to compare. A reviewer must confirm or clear.
rules.basis: QCB AML/CFT Instructions 10.4 (ongoing check against UNSC and NCTC lists); QFCRA sanctions guidance para 16-21 (alert review and records)

rules.title: High-confidence name match, DOB differs
rules.reason: Name matches a listed person but the date of birth differs: probable namesake. Record the disposition with the DOB evidence.
rules.basis: QFCRA sanctions guidance (fuzzy matching calibrated to risk; records of cleared false positives kept)

rules.title: Medium-confidence match
rules.reason: Medium-confidence name similarity to a listed person. Reviewer decides with nationality and DOB evidence.
rules.basis: Firm screening procedure

rules.title: Matched on a listed alias
rules.reason: The hit was on an alias rather than the primary listed name; show the reviewer which alias.
rules.basis: Wolfsberg sanctions screening guidance (alias coverage)

rules.title: Single-name customer without a date of birth
rules.reason: A single-token name cannot be screened meaningfully without a date of birth. Obtain DOB from the ID before onboarding.
rules.basis: Firm screening procedure; common on South Asian corridors

rules.title: Qatar ID birth year does not match stated DOB
rules.reason: The birth year encoded in the QID number differs from the date of birth supplied. Possible data entry error or borrowed identity.
rules.basis: QID number structure

rules.title: Qatar ID nationality does not match stated nationality
rules.reason: The nationality encoded in the QID number differs from the nationality supplied.
rules.basis: QID number structure

rules.title: Identity number is not well-formed
rules.reason: The identity number does not match the published format for that document. Check for a typo before assuming fraud.
rules.basis: Document format specifications

rules.title: Required onboarding fields missing
rules.reason: One or more fields the corridor requires for CDD are missing.
rules.basis: QCB AML/CFT Instructions 15.2 (identification data for individuals); Law 20/2019 CDD

rules.title: Identity document expired
rules.reason: The identity document has expired. A valid document is required before onboarding.
rules.basis: FATF R.10 reliable, independent source documents

rules.title: Selfie does not match the document photo
rules.reason: Face comparison between selfie and document failed. Manual verification required; possible third-party use of a worker's ID.
rules.basis: Firm CDD procedure; corridor typology (borrowed identity)

rules.title: Customer from a FATF call-for-action jurisdiction
rules.reason: Enhanced due diligence required for customers connected to a jurisdiction subject to a FATF call for action.
rules.basis: FATF R.19; QCB AML/CFT Instructions on high-risk countries (cite section after review)

rules.title: Beneficiary identity number not well-formed
rules.reason: The beneficiary ID number does not match the Philippine format given. Correct before sending, or the payout partner will reject.
rules.basis: FATF R.16 beneficiary information; payout partner requirements

rules.title: Beneficiary record incomplete
rules.reason: The beneficiary record lacks fields the receiving side requires.
rules.basis: FATF R.16

rules.title: Sender under 18
rules.reason: Sender is a minor.
rules.basis: Firm policy (confirm minimum age with QCB instructions)

rules.title: Transfer above QR 3,500 requires full CDD
rules.reason: QCB requires customer due diligence for money or value transfers above QR 3,500; identification data is incomplete for this sender.
rules.basis: QCB AML/CFT Instructions, CDD triggers (MVTS above QR 3,500); 18(5)-(6) originator information

rules.title: One-off transaction at or above QR 50,000
rules.reason: Large one-off transaction at or above the QR 50,000 CDD threshold. Verify source of funds; check for linked transactions intended to stay below the threshold.
rules.basis: QCB AML/CFT Instructions CDD triggers (one-off transaction of at least QR 50,000) and 14.12 (linked one-off transactions)

rules.title: Transfer for a charitable cause
rules.reason: QCB prohibits transfers of any value for charitable causes through an MVTS without prior approval from the relevant authority. Hold until approval is evidenced.
rules.basis: QCB AML/CFT Instructions 18(10)

rules.title: Politically exposed person
rules.reason: Customer is a politically exposed person (or family member or close associate to the second degree). Enhanced due diligence, source of wealth and funds, senior management approval.
rules.basis: QCB AML/CFT Instructions 10.3 (measures for PEPs); FATF R.12

rules.title: Non-resident sender without a passport number
rules.reason: QCB identification data requires the QID number for Qataris and residents and the passport number for non-residents.
rules.basis: QCB AML/CFT Instructions 15.2

rules.title: Pay-out above PHP 500,000 on the receiving side
rules.reason: Pay-outs above PHP 500,000 require enhanced due diligence by the paying partner and may only be paid by cheque or credit to an account, not cash. Confirm the payout channel with the partner and complete EDD before sending.
rules.basis: BSP Circular 1206 (2024), regulation on large value pay-outs; AMLC covered transaction reporting above PHP 500,000
